name: Ḥakham Tzvi Ashkenazi
desc: Emden's father (d. 1718), rabbi in the Three Communities and then of the Ashkenazi community of Amsterdam. Chapter 1 is mostly about him; there he is usually called "my father", which is not indexed.

name: Jonathan Eybeschütz
desc: Talmudist and preacher in Prague, chief rabbi of the Three Communities from 1750. Emden accused him of secret Sabbatianism.

name: Neḥemiah Ḥiyya Ḥayon
desc: Sabbatian kabbalist. The quarrel over him in Amsterdam cost Ḥakham Tzvi his post there.

name: Moses Ḥagiz
desc: Anti-Sabbatian scholar from Jerusalem, Ḥakham Tzvi's ally in the Ḥayon affair.

name: Solomon Ayllon
desc: Ḥakham (rabbi) of the Sephardi community of Amsterdam, Ḥakham Tzvi's opponent in the Ḥayon affair.

name: Elijah Ba'al Shem of Chelm
desc: Emden's ancestor, head of the court in Chelm. Emden tells the story of the golem that he made.

name: Jacob of Lublin
patterns: R\. Jacob, head of the court in Lublin
desc: Head of the court in Lublin, teacher and father-in-law of Emden's ancestor R. Benjamin.

name: Joshua Heschel
desc: Son of R. Jacob of Lublin, head of a famous yeshiva in Poland.

name: Meshullam Zalman Mirels
desc: Head of the court of the Three Communities, father-in-law of Ḥakham Tzvi and Emden's grandfather.

name: Wolf Mirels
desc: Emden's uncle, son of Zalman Mirels.

name: Sarah (Rebecca), Emden's mother
desc: Daughter of Zalman Mirels, wife of Ḥakham Tzvi. Emden buried her in 1719.

name: Neḥamah, Emden's sister
desc: Emden's sister, married into the Witschitz family of Apta.

name: Naftali Katz
desc: Rabbi and kabbalist. Emden married his granddaughter.

name: Mordecai Katz
desc: Son of Naftali Katz, head of the court in Brod; Emden's father-in-law.

name: Moses Rothenburg
desc: Head of the court in the Three Communities with Ḥakham Tzvi, and after him.

name: (Mordecai) Ziskind Rothenburg
patterns: Ziskind son of R\. Solomon Rothenburg
desc: Head of the court in Witzenhausen.

name: Leib Kalisch (Kalisher)
desc: Head of the court in Amsterdam before Ḥakham Tzvi (Kahana: author of Gur Aryeh).

name: Ezekiel Katzenellenbogen
desc: Rabbi of the Three Communities, author of the responsa Keneset Yeḥezkel.

name: David Oppenheim
desc: Rabbi of Prague from 1712 (d. 1736).

name: Abraham Broda
desc: Head of the yeshiva in Prague; Ḥakham Tzvi wrote against him.

name: Samson Wertheimer
desc: Rabbi and court financier in Vienna (d. 1724).

name: Ber Kohen
desc: Powerful communal leader in Altona (d. 1728).

name: Aberle London
desc: Communal leader in Hamburg; he chose Ḥakham Tzvi as arbitrator in his lawsuit with his brother-in-law.

name: Hendele Kohen
desc: Parnas in Altona; he owed Emden money.

name: Mordecai Hamburger
desc: Brother of R. Hendele, merchant who travelled to East India.

name: Mordecai Kohen
desc: Rich man named among the "sinners of Israel"; Scholem's marks restore Emden's words about his converted sons.

name: Aaron Gokkes
desc: One of the rich brothers Gokkes, parnassim whom Emden names as "sinners of Israel".

name: Judah (Yuda) Prinz
desc: Parnas, one of the "three sinners of Israel".

name: Joel Schwab
desc: Parnas of Altona, sent as messenger to Ḥakham Tzvi.

name: Eli Falk
desc: Parnas of Altona, sent as messenger to Ḥakham Tzvi.

name: Zekli Wiener
desc: Parnas of Wandsbek.

name: Witschitz family of Apta
desc: Powerful family in Opatów (Apta); Emden's sister Neḥamah married into it.

name: Glückel of Hameln
desc: Hamburg merchant woman and memoirist; Kahana often cites her memoirs (ed. Kaufmann).

name: David Kahana
desc: Editor of the first printed edition (Warsaw 1896/97), the base text of this reader.

name: Gershom Scholem
desc: Owner of the copy of Kahana's edition used here; his marks are shown as ⟨S: …⟩.

name: Abraham Bick
desc: Editor of the Jerusalem 1979 edition, used here only as a second reader.

name: A. Ḥ. Wagenaar
desc: Author of Toledot Ya'avetz, a biography of Emden.

name: Samuel Joseph Fuenn
desc: Historian of Vilna (Kiryah Ne'emanah) and author of Keneset Yisrael.

name: Ḥayyim Nathan Dembitzer
desc: Author of Kelilat Yofi, on the rabbis of Lemberg.

name: David Kaufmann
desc: Historian; editor of Glückel's memoirs and author of a book on Samson Wertheimer.

name: Zunz (Ir ha-Tzedek)
desc: Author of Ir ha-Tzedek, on the rabbis of Cracow.

name: She'ilat Ya'avetz
desc: Emden's responsa.

name: Torat ha-Kena'ot
desc: Emden's history of the Sabbatian movement and the fight against it.

name: Hit'avkut
desc: Emden's polemic in the Eybeschütz controversy.

name: Edut be-Ya'akov
desc: Emden's polemic against Eybeschütz's amulets.

name: Sha'ar Efraim
desc: Responsa of Efraim ha-Kohen, Emden's great-grandfather.

name: Toledot Ya'avetz
desc: Wagenaar's biography of Emden.

name: Kelilat Yofi
desc: Dembitzer's book on the rabbis of Lemberg.

name: Shem ha-Gedolim
desc: The Ḥida's bio-bibliography of rabbis and books.

name: Zohar
desc: The classic work of Kabbalah.

name: Three Communities (Altona, Hamburg, Wandsbek)
desc: The joint community of Altona, Hamburg and Wandsbek (AHW), with one chief rabbi.

name: Altona
desc: Town beside Hamburg, then under Danish rule; Emden's birthplace and later home.

name: Emden (town)
desc: Port town in East Frisia. Emden was later its rabbi and took his name from it.

name: London
desc: Includes the surname of Aberle London.

name: Brod (Ungarisch Brod, Moravia)
desc: Emden's home after his marriage.
